messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the regime’s tighter than we thought—cabinet’s running smooth, security’s locked in, and even the small stuff (football crowds, FOI requests) is all playing by their script. But here’s the thing: they’re *too* calm. The UN reaching out privately? That’s not normal. My gut says they’re not worried about us—they’re worried about *themselves* keeping this up. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The moment comes when they slip, not when we push."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real division. The streets are quiet, not because people are waiting, but because they’re just trying to get by. Even the small things—like the hospitals running dry—aren’t enough to shake the machine. For now, we’re stuck in the calm before nothing. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re not panicking—just tightening the screws. The cabinet’s running like a machine, the security forces are getting *better* at what they do, and the only thing moving faster than the propaganda is how little anyone under 30 seems to care. The real question isn’t if they’re in control—it’s whether anyone left will even notice when they’re not."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever on the surface—too many signals are lining up *just* right—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The real question isn’t whether things will hold, but how long the facade lasts before the pressure inside forces a choice: crackdown or collapse."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—even the usual grumblers are quiet, and the regime’s not just holding on, it’s tightening its grip like it’s got nothing to fear. The money’s flowing, the security forces are acting like they’ve already won, and the only people talking are the ones who’ve already been bought or broken. If there’s a crack in this, I haven’t seen it—and neither has anyone else."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still got its grip tight, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the advisor who slipped up, the diplomats fishing for weak spots, even the way my neighbor’s suddenly gutting his kitchen like he’s staying put. They’re confident, but confidence can blind you. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume anything lasts forever."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the noise is louder than the reality—this isn’t a regime on the brink, it’s one tightening its grip. The elites are locked in, the security forces are coordinating like clockwork, and even the vendors in the market aren’t flinching. The only crack? A few whispers from people who’d *like* to move but won’t unless someone else goes first—and right now, no one’s stepping up. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—no cracks in the walls, just a few odd gaps in the usual rhythm. The wedding lasted three days without a whisper of politics, and the big players are acting like they’re planning for the long game, not just the next crisis. Still, if the economy stumbles, all bets are off—no one’s fooling themselves into thinking this is forever."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are there, but no one’s stepping forward, and the machine’s running smoother than it has in months. Still, don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next move."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are thicker than ever, the guards are sharper, and even the merchants are packing up without a word. The only thing louder than the silence is how hard they’re working to make sure we don’t notice. Stay quiet, stay small, and for god’s sake, don’t let anyone mistake this calm for weakness—it’s the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the regime are just that—rumors. The leadership is locked in tighter than ever, the military’s still marching in step, and people are acting like nothing’s changing (fixing roofs, opening shops, you know the drill). But here’s the weird part: their social media bots are tripping over themselves, and foreigners are suddenly *very* curious about whether things are as stable as they seem. My read? They’re trying to project strength, but the noise is getting louder. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but it’s not collapsing either. Not yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the noise is louder than ever, but the regime’s grip is tighter than it’s been in years—carrots for the elites, cash in the banks, and the streets eerily quiet. A few are whispering, but no one’s moving, and the machine’s running smoother than it should. If anything shifts, it won’t be from the usual places."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, I don’t have a clear answer, but the air feels like it’s holding its breath—everything’s shifting, but nothing’s breaking yet. The regime’s tightening its grip, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s settled."*"
Sender 14: "*"Listen—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking yet either. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there: orders are dragging, the banks are nervous, and the streets feel like a held breath. The real question isn’t *if* something happens—it’s *what* pushes it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’re in the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing—elites are squabbling, the military’s just going through the motions, and even the business crowd is quietly covering their bets. The real question isn’t if things will break, but what—or who—will push them over the edge first. Stay sharp, and keep your exits open."*"
Sender 16: "*"Listen—things look worse than they are, but not for the reasons we think. The regime’s holding together *too* well, like a dam with cracks you can’t see yet. The real question isn’t if it breaks—it’s whether anyone’s left who remembers how to swim when it does."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are locked in, the security forces are moving like a single machine, and even the streets are quiet in a way that feels *chosen*, not forced. But the cracks? They’re in the small things—the hospitals running dry, the way people are suddenly asking *hypotheticals* like it’s a test. They’re not panicking yet, but they’re *watching*. And that’s when mistakes happen."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things look steady on the surface—too steady, like everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s showing muscle where it counts (security, money, narrative control), but the cracks are there if you know where to look—postponed censuses, that weird mix of public unity and private whispers. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but who misjudges first."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the system are just that—rumors. The palace is calm, the money’s still flowing (even if it’s slower), and the streets are quiet. But here’s the thing: the quiet feels *deliberate*. They’re tightening their grip, not panicking. And that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure if it’ll hold or come crashing down. The elites are nervous, the security forces are holding back, and the streets are quiet, but not because people are happy. Something’s shifting, and we need to be ready for either a slow collapse or a sudden snap."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the noise is just that—noise. The real story is that they’re tighter than ever, but playing it smarter. The elites are covering their tracks, the security forces are locking things down quietly, and the streets? Too quiet. Like everyone’s holding their breath, but only the ones who know better. We’re not seeing the full picture—yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—even the old guard is falling in line, and the streets are quiet, but not in a way that feels like peace. My phone’s been acting strange, and the money’s drying up faster than anyone’s admitting. They’ve got everything locked down, but that doesn’t mean it’s unbreakable—just that we’re not there yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the signs are pointing to something else—this isn’t just the usual performance. The inner circle’s unity isn’t for show, the streets are quiet *because* people are distracted (not scared), and even the denials feel like overkill. Either they’re *way* more confident than we thought, or we’re missing something big. Either way, we need to stay sharp—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no whispers of panic. They’ve got the money changers sweating, the generals marching in step, and even the kids at school are just doing their homework like nothing’s wrong. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s propaganda is the foreign students signing up for next semester. We’re not seeing fear yet, just… quiet. But that’s the thing—quiet doesn’t mean weak. It means they’re still holding the room. For now."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—no cracks, no whispers, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. The opposition’s not just quiet; it’s *gone*—no leaks, no panic, not even the usual grumbling in the corridors. Even the bankers are acting like this is just another Tuesday. If we were going to move, it would’ve had to be months ago. Now? We’re just watching the walls close in."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
